title: 第五章 苔痕第六章 石上迹
content_zh:
雨又接连下了两日，才终于有了放晴的迹象。
潮湿阴冷的通铺里，病倒的杂役又多了几个。王虎的烧退了些，但咳得厉害，脸色蜡黄，每日只能喝点稀粥。陈默每日做完分内的活计，会顺手帮他把水缸挑满，偶尔将自己那份硬馒头掰开，泡软了递给他一半。王虎哑着嗓子道谢，眼神灰败，再也没提过下个月外门小比的事。
陈默的生活依旧被那卷日课纸精确切割。寅时三刻起身，站桩。卯时上山砍柴，用那把越磨越利的柴刀。白日里各种繁重劳作。戌时之后的时光，如今却悄然多了一点内容。
他先是在那背风的屋檐下（雨水已退，地面被连日细雨浸得颜色深暗），就着最后的天光，再次翻看那本丹药笔记。这一次，他看得更加仔细，不再试图记住那些陌生的丹药名称，而是专注于最前面的几页——那里详细罗列了十几种青云山脉外围常见、低阶修士偶尔会用到的草药和矿物，并附有粗糙但清晰的手绘图形、采摘时令、简单的保存和粗加工方法。
“止血藤，多生于向阳崖壁石缝，茎呈暗红，断面有淡红汁液，叶椭圆带锯齿。取其茎皮捣烂外敷，可收敛普通外伤出血，效力微弱，胜于凡俗金疮药。”
“铁骨草，溪边阴湿处常见，叶窄而硬，边缘有细密倒刺，根部深扎，呈铁锈色。取根部晒干研磨，温水冲服，可微弱强健筋骨，长期服用稍有裨益，然味道苦涩，多有杂质，需慎用。”
“青礞石，溪涧底或山洪冲积处可得，色青灰，质脆，断面有玻璃光泽。捣碎成粉，可作低阶丹药‘清心散’辅料，亦可微量掺入符墨，增强基础‘静心符’稳定性，然杂质多，效力不纯，大宗交易不取。”
……
陈默的目光，在“铁骨草”和“青礞石”的条目上，多停留了片刻。尤其是铁骨草，描述中“微弱强健筋骨”、“长期服用稍有裨益”的字样，让他心头微动。《基础淬体术》练了这么久，进步缓慢得让人绝望，任何一点可能的助力，都显得弥足珍贵。而青礞石，虽主要是丹药符箓材料，但那“静心”的描述，让他联想到自己炼气吐纳时，杂念丛生、难以静心的困境。
他将这几页反复看了几遍，直到天色完全暗透，字迹模糊难辨，才将册子小心收起。
然后，他开始尝试那本体术残篇上的动作。
五个动作，依旧残缺不全，注解含糊。他先练第一个，那个需要手臂反拧、单腿独立的别扭姿势。他摆好架势，立刻感受到肩关节和背部肌肉传来的、强烈的撕扯感，比前日尝试时更清晰。他努力维持着，按照图谱上那歪歪扭扭的线条，调整身体的角度，同时心里默念着旁边那语焉不详的“气贯双臂”的提示。
何为“气”？是吐纳时那缕微弱暖流吗？那暖流至今连胸口都难以突破，更遑论“贯”入双臂。他只能依靠纯粹的肌肉力量去维持这个姿势，去感受那种深入筋腱的拉伸。
三息，五息，七息……
汗水从额角渗出，手臂开始无法控制地颤抖。他咬紧牙关，又坚持了两息，终于力竭，踉跄着放下手臂，大口喘气，肩关节处传来火辣辣的酸痛。
他没有立刻休息，而是换到另一边，尝试镜像动作。同样艰难，同样只能坚持短短数息。
第一个动作做完，他已是大汗淋漓，比砍半天柴还要累。他没有冒进，而是盘膝坐下，开始每晚的炼气吐纳，试图平复紊乱的呼吸和悸动的气血。
今夜的气感，似乎比往日更加微弱，丹田空空，那缕暖意迟迟不见踪影。或许是因为方才尝试体术，耗费了太多精力，也扰乱了心神。陈默并不气馁，只是静心守意，在黑暗和寂静中，一遍遍运行着那套早已熟极而流的吐纳法门。
直到子时将至，那股微弱的暖意，才姗姗来迟。依旧孱弱，依旧在胸口滞涩不前，但陈默能感觉到，今夜这暖意流经手臂附近时，似乎……那因练习体术而酸胀僵硬的筋肉，传来一丝极其微弱的、仿佛被温热湿布轻轻拂过的舒缓感。
很轻微，轻微到可能是错觉。

但他记住了这种感觉。
两日后，天终于放晴。久违的阳光刺破云层，洒在湿漉漉的杂役院，蒸腾起氤氲的水汽。被阴雨困了多日的杂役们，脸上也多了些活气，虽然活计并不会因此减少半分。
午后，陈默被派去后山另一处林地，清理一片被风雨刮倒的树木。和他同去的还有另外三个杂役，其中就有那个曾和他一起清理杂草、提起外门小比的王虎。王虎病好了大半，但人依旧有些蔫，不怎么说话。
倒伏的树木不小，枝杈纵横，清理起来颇费功夫。四人用柴刀、斧头，又砍又劈，忙活了近两个时辰，才将主干锯断，枝杈清理得差不多。
“歇会儿，歇会儿，累死老子了。”一个叫李大的壮实杂役一屁股坐在一段树干上，抹了把汗。
另一个杂役也坐下来，从怀里摸出个干硬的饼子啃着。
王虎靠在一棵树旁，脸色还是有些发白，微微喘气。
陈默没有立刻休息，他提着柴刀，走到林地边缘。这里靠近一条从山上流下来的小溪，雨后溪水丰沛，哗哗流淌。溪边乱石嶙峋，生着茂密的喜湿植物。
他的目光，在溪边的草丛石缝间逡巡。
忽然，他停下脚步。在几块湿滑的青石缝隙里，他看到了一丛叶片窄硬、边缘带着细密倒刺的野草。草茎不高，根部附近的泥土颜色较深。
铁骨草。
和笔记上画的图形，有七八分相似。
content_en:
It rained for two more days before finally showing signs of clearing up.
In the damp and cold main shop, a few more handymen fell ill. Wang Hu's fever has gone down a bit, but he has a severe cough and his face is sallow. He can only drink some gruel every day. After Chen Mo finished his assigned work every day, he would help him fill the water tank. Occasionally, he would break off his share of hard steamed buns, soften them and hand half to him. Wang Hu thanked him in a hoarse voice, with gray eyes, and never mentioned the external competition next month.
Chen Mo's life is still accurately cut by that roll of daily school paper. At three o'clock in the morning, he stood up and stood up. When I go up the mountain to chop firewood, I use the hatchet that gets sharper and sharper. All kinds of heavy work during the day. The time after Xu Shi now quietly has a little more content.
He first looked at the elixir notebook under the leeward eaves (the rain had receded and the ground was darkened by the continuous drizzle), using the last light of daylight. This time, he looked more carefully, no longer trying to remember the names of the unfamiliar elixirs, but focused on the first few pages - there was a detailed list of more than a dozen herbs and minerals that were common around the Qingyun Mountains and occasionally used by low-level monks, with rough but clear hand-drawn graphics, picking seasons, simple preservation and rough processing methods.
"Hemostatic Vine grows mostly in the rock crevices of Xiangyang cliffs. The stems are dark red, with light red sap in the cross section, and the leaves are oval and serrated. Take the bark of the stem and pound it for external application. It can stop bleeding from ordinary trauma. The effect is weak, and it is better than ordinary sore medicine."
"Temple grass is commonly found in damp and shady places by streams. Its leaves are narrow and hard, with fine barbs on the edges. The roots are deep-rooted and are rust-colored. Dry and grind the roots, and drink it with warm water. It can weakly strengthen muscles and bones. Long-term use is slightly beneficial. However, it tastes bitter and contains many impurities, so it should be used with caution."
"Qingren stone can be found at the bottom of streams or in alluvial areas of mountain torrents. It is blue-grey in color, brittle in texture, and has a glass luster in its cross-section. Crush it into powder and can be used as an auxiliary material for the low-level elixir 'Qingxin Powder'. It can also be mixed with a trace amount of talisman ink to enhance the stability of the basic 'Jingxin Talisman'. However, it has many impurities and is not pure in effectiveness, so it is not suitable for large-scale transactions."
…
Chen Mo's eyes lingered on the entries for "Iron Bone Grass" and "Qingzhen Stone" for a moment longer. Especially for Iron Bone Grass, the words "weakly strengthens muscles and bones" and "long-term use may be slightly beneficial" in the description made his heart move slightly. After practicing "Basic Body Tempering Technique" for so long, the progress is hopelessly slow. Any possible help is precious. Although Qingren Stone is mainly the material for elixir talismans, the description of "quiet mind" reminded him of the dilemma of being surrounded by distracting thoughts and unable to meditate when he was refining qi and breathing out.
He read these pages several times until it was completely dark and the writing was blurry and difficult to read, then he carefully put the book away.
Then, he began to try the movements in the remaining part of the body technique.
The five movements are still incomplete and the annotations are vague. He practiced the first one first, the awkward posture that required twisting the arms behind his back and making one leg independent. He took up his stance and immediately felt a strong tearing sensation from his shoulder joints and back muscles, which was clearer than when he tried it the day before. He tried hard to maintain it, adjusting the angle of his body according to the crooked lines on the map, and at the same time silently recited the vague "Qi through both arms" prompt next to him.
What is "qi"? Is it the weak warm current when breathing in and out? The warmth has been difficult to break through even the chest, let alone penetrate into the arms. He could only rely on pure muscle strength to maintain this posture and feel the stretch that penetrated deep into the tendons.
Three breaths, five breaths, seven breaths...
Sweat dripped from his forehead, and his arms began to shake uncontrollably. He gritted his teeth and held on for two more breaths. Finally, exhausted, he staggered and lowered his arms, gasping for air, feeling burning pain in his shoulder joints.
Instead of resting immediately, he switched to the other side and tried a mirror move. It's just as difficult, and it can only last for a few breaths.
After finishing the first movement, he was already sweating profusely, and it took him more than half a day to chop firewood.Still tired. Instead of rushing forward, he sat down cross-legged and began to practice Qi refining and breathing every night, trying to calm his disordered breathing and throbbing Qi and blood.
Tonight, the sense of energy seems to be weaker than in the past, the dantian is empty, and the warmth has been missing. Perhaps it was because he had just tried physical skills, which consumed too much energy and disturbed his mind. Chen Mo was not discouraged, he just kept his mind calm, and in the darkness and silence, he ran the already familiar breathing method over and over again.
It was not until midnight that the faint warmth came. It was still weak and still stagnant in his chest, but Chen Mo could feel that when the warmth flowed through his arms tonight, it seemed that... the muscles that were sore and stiff from practicing physical skills felt an extremely weak sense of relief, as if they were gently brushed by a warm wet cloth.
It's very slight, so slight that it might be an illusion.
But he remembered the feeling.
Two days later, the sky finally cleared. The long-lost sunshine pierced the clouds and sprinkled the wet courtyard, evaporating dense water vapor. The handymen who have been trapped in the rain for many days also have a little more energy on their faces, although their work will not be reduced by half.
In the afternoon, Chen Mo was sent to another woodland in the back mountain to clean up a tree that had been knocked down by wind and rain. There were three other handymen who went with him, including Wang Hu, who had cleaned weeds with him and talked about the outer door competition. Wang Hu has mostly recovered from his illness, but he is still a little weak and doesn't talk much.
The fallen trees were quite large and had tangled branches, so it took a lot of effort to clean them up. The four people used hatchets and axes to chop and split. After working for nearly two hours, they sawed off the main trunk and almost cleared the branches.
"Take a rest, take a rest, I'm exhausted." A sturdy handyman named Li Da sat down on a tree trunk and wiped his sweat.
Another handyman also sat down, took out a dry and hard pancake from his arms and gnawed on it.
Wang Hu leaned against a tree, his face still a little pale, and he was breathing slightly.
Chen Mo did not rest immediately. He carried the hatchet and walked to the edge of the forest. Here is close to a small stream flowing down from the mountain. After the rain, the water in the stream is abundant and flowing. The rocks beside the stream are rugged and densely covered with moisture-loving plants.
His eyes wandered among the grass and rocks beside the stream.
Suddenly, he stopped. In the gaps between some slippery bluestones, he saw a clump of weeds with narrow, hard leaves and fine barbs on the edges. The grass stems are not high, and the soil near the roots is darker.
Irongrass.
It is 70% or 80% similar to the graphics drawn in the notes.
